mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns higher over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 4% but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When both employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) show concurrent increases, it indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases, it signals tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increase but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS drops below 500,000 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
